messages.subject: passing values to updateNumericInput
parts:
I have a numericInput, and I cannot understand how its value is set by updateNumericInput.  I'll show you the code that I don't understand, and then explain it.  The code looks like this:

 observe({modelPNRR <<- input$modelPNRR

     if (modelPNRR) {

              enableActionButton("getPNRR", session)

               enableActionButton("pnrrAdj", session)

      } else {

              disableActionButton("getPNRR", session)

              disableActionButton("pnrrAdj", session)

     }

})


observe({pnrrAdjustment <<- input$pnrrAdj})

observe({if (modelPNRR && input$getPNRR > 0) {

     # start a progress message

     y <- getPNRR(.95)

     print(paste("value returned for pnrr is ", y))

     updateNumericInput(session, "pnrrAdj", value = y)

     # updateNumericInput(session, "pnrrAdj", value = 25)      # this updates the value

})

The modelPNRR variable turns this part of the program off and on, so input$modelPNRR is a checkbox.  When it is checked, the program uses a variable called pnrrAdjustment, which can be set by the user, or calculated.  So modelPNRR enables a numericInput (input$pnrrAdj) for the user to set the value, and also enables an action button (input$getPNRR)

pnrrAdjustment is defined in the environment of the server function. The getPNRR function calculates and sets its value, and returns the value set.  The calculation is iterative, so it is set multiple times during the getPNRR call.  In the code shown, the updateNumericInput call fails - the value is not set in the input control, but the observe on input$pnrrAdj is apparently being triggered, because the pnrrAdjustment variable in my program is being set to NA.  print statement is showing the right value, and the updateNumericInput call that I've commented out does set a value.  

I feel like this must be something simple that I am unable to see.
